2. Cohort Retention

Customers are grouped by first-purchase month. Retention rate = fraction of cohort that purchased again in each subsequent month.

⚠ Overall Month-1 retention (16.1%) is below the 20% guardrail.

3. Guardrail, Month-1 Retention by Channel

Month-1 retention below 20% signals acquisition of customers with no genuine purchase intent.

✓ Enthusiast: 31.0% Month-1 retention, above guardrail.
✗ Deal-Seeker: 4.5% Month-1 retention, GUARDRAIL BREACHED. Expanding flash-sale acquisition destroys retention economics.
✗ Mainstream: 13.0% Month-1 retention, also below guardrail. Audit acquisition mix.

4. RFM Segmentation

Each customer receives R, F, and M scores (1–5). The (R, F) combination maps to one of 11 named segments.

ℹ The M score creates a conflict: Deal-Seekers rank highest on M (large first basket) but lowest on predicted CLV. See Section 7.

5. BG/NBD Purchase Frequency Model

The BG/NBD model was fit on the calibration period and validated on the 91-day holdout. Parameters:

ParameterValueInterpretation
r (purchase rate shape)0.7083Moderate purchase rate heterogeneity
α (purchase rate scale)98.63Slow baseline rate, expected for non-subscription retail
a (dropout shape)0.2118Low individual variation in churn
b (dropout scale)1.3753Mean dropout ≈ 13.4% per purchase

6. 12-Month CLV Prediction

Combining BG/NBD and Gamma-Gamma gives a discounted 12-month CLV per customer. Customers with a single purchase (frequency = 0) receive CLV = 0, correct model behaviour.

7. The Tension, M Score vs Predicted CLV

Deal-Seekers rank highest on RFM Monetary score (high historical spend) but lowest on predicted CLV. This is the analytical crux: the naive M-score ranking inverts the CLV ranking.

✗ A win-back campaign ranked by M score would contact Deal-Seekers first, the channel with the worst ROI and the lowest retention.

8. Holdout Validation

BG/NBD predictions for the 91-day holdout period versus actual purchases.

✓ Overall holdout MAE = 0.4745 purchases/customer. Bias = +0.0348 (slightly optimistic).

9. CLV by Acquisition Channel

Violin plots show the full CLV distribution per channel, not just means. A narrow Enthusiast distribution means high CLV is broad-based, not outlier-driven.

✓ Enthusiast mean CLV £255.26 is 5.3× Deal-Seeker mean CLV £48.60.

10. Win-Back Campaign ROI

£3.50 cost per contact, channel-specific response rates (Enthusiast 18%, Mainstream 9%, Deal-Seeker 4%).

✓ Enthusiast ROI: +10.0× per contact. Budget spend on Enthusiasts returns £38.50 per £3.50 contact.
⚠ Mainstream ROI: +1.61× per contact. Positive but modest, existing customers worth retaining, acquisition worth auditing.
✗ Deal-Seeker ROI: -0.49× per contact. NEGATIVE, each contact loses £1.70 on a £3.50 outreach.
